solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Rabat and Beirut, after negotiations, calmer?

indicators.note: after negotiations the two capitals' letters have been bargained into a new order

explanation.surface: Morocco and Lebanon, once talks are over, feel more relaxed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'calmer' looks like an adjective about the two cities, but it is a noun: something that calms you, with the question mark flagging the example.
explanation.definitionFit: A sedative drug is something that calms the patient, so it is a calmer in a punning sense.

clue.text: A vehicle rolling over breaking a number of times, pull in

indicators.note: breaking means bursting into, so the reversed vehicle goes inside

parts.note: T is the abbreviation for times, here two of them

indicators.note: rolling over means the vehicle is turned upside down, so read backwards in a down light

parts.note: a cart is a vehicle

explanation.surface: A car overturning repeatedly draws a crowd.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rolling over' reverses the vehicle, and 'breaking' puts it between the two Ts; T is the standard abbreviation for times, as in multiplication.
explanation.definitionFit: To draw in or lure people, as a magnet or a show draws a crowd.

clue.text: Cocktail maker demonstrating skill during drinking session

indicators.note: during means in the middle of, so the skill goes inside the session

parts.note: a bender is a drinking spree
art is skill

explanation.surface: A mixologist shows off talent at a boozy party.
explanation.definitionFit: The person behind a bar mixes and serves drinks, including mixed cocktails.

clue.text: Emperor has to go with uprising, defeat at last accepted

indicators.note: accepted means taken in, so the reversed word holds the next letter
uprising means going up, so in a down light the letters are read backwards

parts.note: to suit is to go with, as a colour matches

indicators.note: at last picks the final letter of the word before it

explanation.surface: An emperor must deal with a revolt, finally accepting defeat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'uprising' turns SUIT into TIUS, which takes in T from the end of 'defeat'.
explanation.definitionFit: A Roman ruler of the Flavian dynasty who completed the Colosseum.

clue.text: For training, I rope in all the players

indicators.note: training means bending into shape, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone ropes in the whole team for practice.
explanation.definitionFit: In baroque music the term means the full orchestra, as opposed to the soloists.

clue.text: Cheat reportedly also needing something to do in prison

indicators.note: reportedly means as heard, so the word for also is replaced by one sounding the same

parts.note: too means also
prisoners do time, serving a sentence

explanation.surface: A cheat is said to need a prison sentence as well.
explanation.definitionFit: To be unfaithful to a partner by seeing someone else, so to cheat on them.

clue.text: Sound bites crude, prepare chamber for entertainment?

indicators.note: bites means holding in the teeth, so the noise surrounds the next word

parts.note: din is a loud sound
raw means crude, unrefined
to groom is to prepare, as for a role

explanation.surface: Coarse soundbites prepare a hall for a show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sound bites' looks like one phrase, media snippets, but splits into a noise that 'bites' (holds in its jaws) the word for crude.
explanation.definitionFit: A room in a grand house where guests are received and entertained, a reception room.

clue.text: Fish, duck and sheep reared

indicators.note: reared means raised up, so in a down light the letters are read upwards

parts.note: a duck in cricket is a score of nil
a ram is a male sheep

explanation.surface: A list of livestock raised on a farm: fish, duck and sheep.
explanation.walkthrough: A duck is a cricketer's score of zero.
explanation.definitionFit: A large game fish with a long spear-like upper jaw, a billfish.

clue.text: Minister covering up a potentially catastrophic device

indicators.note: covering up says the minister's title wraps around the letter that follows

parts.note: a rector is a parish minister in the church

explanation.surface: A government minister hushes up a dangerous gadget.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Minister' suggests a politician, but it is the church sense: a rector.
explanation.definitionFit: A nuclear plant's core can melt down disastrously, so it is a device that could cause catastrophe.

clue.text: Best sink hole put back!

indicators.note: put back says the pair of words is written in reverse order, letter by letter

parts.note: to pot a ball in snooker is to sink it
a pit is a hole in the ground

explanation.surface: An instruction to restore a sinkhole, praised as excellent.
explanation.definitionFit: Something first-rate or excellent is the best, a colloquial superlative.

clue.text: Sporting moment captured in glossy perhaps?

definitions.text: Sporting moment captured in glossy perhaps?

parts.words: Sporting moment captured in glossy perhaps?
parts.note: a race so close it needs a camera to decide; a glossy print has a shiny coating on its surface

explanation.surface: A sports moment caught in a glossy magazine.
explanation.walkthrough: Two senses at once: the camera-judged end of a close race, and the coating of a print, gloss or matt.
explanation.definitionFit: A neck-and-neck race result decided by a camera at the line, and also a print's surface coating.

clue.text: In retirement, time passed swiftly in good health

indicators.note: retirement is a going back, so the letters are read backwards

parts.note: an era is a period of time
time that passed swiftly flew

explanation.surface: A retiree finds time has raced by while staying healthy.
explanation.definitionFit: Wellbeing, health and prosperity are what the word means, so good health fits.

clue.text: European doctor wished to follow instructions, finally

indicators.note: to follow says the rearranged word comes after the single picked letter
finally picks the closing letter of the word that follows
to doctor something is to tamper with it, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A physician hoped to obey orders to the end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'doctor' looks like the physician but is the anagram signal: WISHED becomes WEDISH, placed after S, the end of 'instructions'.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone from Sweden is a European, a national of a European country.

clue.text: Group unable to score?

definitions.meaning: a set of nine performers or things
with ... there is nowhere to put the ball, so no goal can be scored

explanation.surface: A band that cannot hit a goal.
explanation.definitionFit: A group of nine musicians is a standard ensemble name, like trio or quartet.

clue.text: Fishy first course on the way

indicators.note: on means the course of a meal is placed against the following pieces

parts.note: a dish is a course of a meal
one is the first number
St is short for street, a way

explanation.surface: A starter served while travelling smells suspicious.
explanation.definitionFit: Fishy is slang for suspicious or underhand, so it means untrustworthy.

clue.text: Something sharp pinning clothes, darned perhaps?

indicators.note: pinning means holding in place, so the blade surrounds the clothes

parts.note: a sword is a sharp blade
wear means clothes, as in evening wear

explanation.surface: A needle pins clothes that have been mended.
explanation.walkthrough: 'darned' looks like mended socks, but it is a mild oath, an example of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A mild curse such as darned is an expletive, a word used in place of cursing.

clue.text: Chaser or otherwise ultimately whipped?

indicators.note: whipped means beaten about, so the letters of the first two words are thrown into a new order
ultimately picks the final letter of the word before it

explanation.surface: A steeplechaser, or a flat runner, is in the end given the whip.
explanation.walkthrough: Whole-clue reading: a jumper ('chaser') or otherwise, this animal ends up being whipped by the jockey.
explanation.definitionFit: A steeplechaser is a jumping thoroughbred, and flat runners are the other kind; both get whipped in a race.

clue.text: Appellation on wine, similar drinks superior

parts.note: cha and tea are two names for the same drink
U means upper-class, superior

explanation.surface: A wine label and the beverages that outclass it.
explanation.definitionFit: French wine labels name the estate, as in Château Margaux, a name printed on the bottle.

clue.text: Woman expecting money say in rise, she flips!

indicators.note: flips means turns head over heels, so the letters are reordered

explanation.surface: A woman awaiting money gets a pay rise and goes wild.
explanation.definitionFit: A female who stands to inherit a fortune is waiting for an inheritance.

clue.text: Utterance from setter perhaps about conclusion of awful writer

indicators.note: about means the dog's noise goes around the next piece

parts.note: a setter is a breed of dog, and a dog's bark is written woof

indicators.note: conclusion of picks the final letter of the word after it

explanation.surface: The crossword compiler bemoans how badly a novelist ends.
explanation.walkthrough: 'setter' looks like the puzzle's compiler but is the dog breed. Virginia Woolf was an English modernist novelist.
explanation.definitionFit: Virginia Woolf wrote novels such as Mrs Dalloway, so she is a writer.

clue.text: Film taking you and I back

parts.note: we means you and I
the stern is the back of a ship

explanation.surface: A movie that takes the two of us home.
explanation.definitionFit: A cowboy picture set in the American frontier is a genre of movie.

clue.text: Prayer kept up by journo's ironic

indicators.note: kept up says the hidden letters are read backwards
by here means held by, so the letters are contained in the words after it

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A journalist's mocking prayer is preserved.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by' signals letters held within 'journo's ironic', and 'kept up' says read them upwards, as this is a down light.
explanation.definitionFit: An old literary word for a spoken petition to God.

clue.text: Leader in orchestra wheels in a small instrument

indicators.note: the leader in a word is its opening letter

parts.note: wheels is slang for a car

explanation.surface: The orchestra's first violinist brings a tiny instrument in on wheels.
explanation.definitionFit: A small egg-shaped wind instrument with finger holes, a little flute-like instrument.

clue.text: A temporary cut in open spaces

indicators.note: cut means the word is shortened, its last letter removed

parts.note: a trial period is temporary

explanation.surface: A short-term reduction in open areas.
explanation.definitionFit: Courtyards in Roman houses, and also hall spaces, plural of an open central court.

clue.text: National broadcast of Iran entertaining American spies originally

indicators.note: entertaining means holding guests inside, so the rearranged letters surround the next pieces
broadcast means scattered about, so these letters are rearranged
originally picks the opening letter of the word before it

explanation.surface: Iranian radio hosts US intelligence agents.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broadcast of' turns IRAN into RIAN, which holds US and S (start of 'spies').
explanation.definitionFit: A citizen of Russia is a national of that country, the noun sense of national.

clue.text: Turn featuring latest characters in the television show

indicators.note: featuring means containing, so the turn wraps around the letters picked out

parts.note: to veer is to turn

indicators.note: the latest characters are the last letters of each of the two following words

explanation.surface: A twist in the latest episode of a TV programme.
explanation.walkthrough: 'show' looks like part of 'television show' but stands alone. EN, the ends of 'the' and 'television', goes in after the V.
explanation.definitionFit: A veneer is a thin outward layer or facade, a mere show over what lies beneath.

clue.text: Difficult little number, uniform short pink dresses

parts.note: one is the smallest whole number

indicators.note: dresses means clothes something, so the shortened colour wraps around the next letter
short means the final letter of the colour is dropped

parts.note: rose is a shade of pink
Uniform is U in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A tricky small dance number has a uniform with pink dresses.
explanation.definitionFit: Burdensome and taxing, a task that is hard work, so difficult.

clue.text: Fine yet to be paid

definitions.meaning: still owing, as with a debt or bill

explanation.surface: A penalty that has not been settled.
explanation.definitionFit: Excellent work is first-rate, and an unpaid debt is still owing; both senses share the word.
